configuration.message: Dear $(n2.inboundWebhook.customerName), Your parcel (reference id: $(n2.inboundWebhook.parcelID)) will be delievered by $(n2.inboundWebhook.delievryTime) on $(n2.inboundWebhook.deliveryDate). Reply within next 24 hours with CANCEL if you'd like to cancel the delivery or with CHANGE if you'd like to change the delivery address.
Thanks for confirming. The delivery for parcel id: $(n2.inboundWebhook.parcelID) has been cancelled.
Sorry, that's an invalid response. Please call our customer service helpline for further assistance.
Thanks for your response. Please respond with the updated delivery address.
Your updated address has been captured as: '$(n31.receive.message)'. Please reply with YES to confirm or else reply with RETRY to submit the address again.
Thanks for confirming. The delivery address has been updated successfully.
Apologies, your delivery could not be cancelled due to some technical error. Please call our customer service helpline for further assistance.
Apologies, your delivery address could not be updated due to some technical error. Please call our customer service helpline for further assistance.

authored_walkthrough.walkthrough: A webhook triggers the delivery SMS, then Receive 4 waits up to 86400 seconds. Branch 5 recognizes CANCEL or CHANGE case-insensitively. CANCEL calls HTTP 15, then sends cancellation confirmation on success or a technical-error message on error. CHANGE asks for an address, waits at Receive 31, echoes that address for confirmation, and waits at Receive 36. YES calls HTTP 41 and sends update confirmation/error; RETRY returns to the address question, making an explicit loop. Other initial answers receive an invalid-response message. Thus the two API actions occur after distinct customer confirmations, rather than merely after sending the first alert.
authored_walkthrough.handoffs: The initial message uses `n2.inboundWebhook.customerName`, `parcelID`, `delievryTime` and `deliveryDate`; recipients use `phoneNumber`. Branches consume `$(n4.receive.message)` and `$(n36.receive.message)`. The proposed address is `$(n31.receive.message)` and is echoed by Send 33 before the YES branch.
authored_walkthrough.limitations: The initial webhook parse schema and business URLs are not operationally populated in this capture. Preserve the misspelled observed `delievryTime` only when matching the actual trigger schema. Several Receive failure/timeout declarations have no captured destination, and the RETRY cycle has no explicit attempt counter. Confirm API body bindings and recovery policy before reuse; customer-facing success text is not delivery/API execution evidence.
